player.name: Sir Bartholomew Puddle
player.concept: a self-appointed knight of the realm, absurdly confident and absurdly wrong
player.build: human paladin 3 (Oath of Devotion), soldier background

established: When the player tried this (Joke that the pigeon did it), it worked: Kell gives the pigeon a brief, dry look, then says, “Noted. The pigeon is not under arrest.” She turns back to her notebook and the yard.

When the player tried this (Ask the girl who strung up Prout), it failed: Moll gives the same story louder, adding that Prout leapt right from the loft door, while Cob barks agreement. Kell notes that the girl claims she saw him jump; her story remains open to challenge.
Sir Bartholomew is on the hoist beam beside Prout
Prout didn't hang himself: what has been found shows he was killed and then hoisted up to look like a suicide.
Prout's body is down from the hoist and has struck the cobbles beside Cob
Moll shows the wheat-ear silver crown she was paid with
Cob refuses to show his crowns or answer about the boots.
Moll moves closer to shield Cob.

rulings.act: Joke that the pigeon did it
rulings.why: they'd do it anyway (trivial, free, wary)
rulings.changed: Kell gives the pigeon a brief, dry look, then says, “Noted. The pigeon is not under arrest.” She turns back to her notebook and the yard

rulings.act: Ask the girl who strung up Prout
rulings.changed: Moll gives the same story louder, adding that Prout leapt right from the loft door, while Cob barks agreement. Kell notes that the girl claims she saw him jump; her story remains open to challenge

rulings.act: Climb the hoist rope to inspect Prout and the loft door
rulings.changed: Sir Bartholomew hauls himself up the rope despite his chain mail and reaches the hoist beam beside Prout. From there, he can inspect the body and the barred loft door at close range

rulings.act: Cut the hoist rope and catch Prout’s body
rulings.changed: The rope parts under Sir Bartholomew's sword, but Prout's weight wrenches free of his grasp and the body strikes the cobbles hard beside Cob. Cob jerks back, dropping his stones, while Kell hurries to the body and begins her examination; came out: not-suicide

rulings.act: Ask Moll what the gentleman looked like and what she is holding
rulings.why: it comes freely when asked (guarded, plausible, wary)
rulings.changed: Moll opens her fist to show a silver crown stamped with a wheat-ear. “His face? Didn’t get a good look. Good coat, silver cane, and enough lavender water to drown in.”

rulings.act: Ask Cob to show his coins and explain the boots
rulings.changed: Cob clenches his fist over the crowns and turns his back, edging toward the water butt. “Cob told you. Found ’em. Quit asking.” Moll steps in closer to shield him, and Kell notes that Cob declined to show the coins or answer further
